svg.title: Hoare partition: conditions, swaps, and the returned boundary
svg.desc: One call to partition of 9, 3, 8, 2, 7 with the saved middle value 8 as pivot. The left scan skips values below 8; the right scan skips values above 8. The first pair is 9 and 7: swap them, then set i to 1 and j to 3. The next left scan skips 3 and stops at 8; the right scan stops at 2. Swap 8 and 2, then set i to 3 and j to 2. The outer loop condition fails. Return j equals 2. Indices 0 through 2 hold 7, 3, 2, all at most 8. Indices 3 through 4 hold 8, 9, all at least 8. The left range still needs sorting.
svg.text: i/j = scan indices. Orange outline = swapped cell.
0. Save the middle value as the pivot
pivot = arr[2] = 8; i = low = 0; j = high = 4.
1. Scan: find values that can switch sides
i: arr[0] < pivot? 9 < 8 is false; stop at i = 0.
j: arr[4] > pivot? 7 > 8 is false; stop at j = 4.
9 is too large for the left; 7 is too small for the right.
i >= j? 0 >= 4 is false; swap arr[0] and arr[4].
7 fits the <= 8 group; 9 fits the >= 8 group.
3. Skip 3: it already fits the left group
i: arr[1] < pivot? 3 < 8 is true; i becomes 2.
i: arr[2] < pivot? 8 < 8 is false; stop at i = 2.
j: arr[3] > pivot? 2 > 8 is false; stop at j = 3.
i >= j? 2 >= 3 is false; swap arr[2] and arr[3].
2 belongs on the left; 8 can go right (equal to pivot).
i <= j? 3 <= 2 is false; leave the outer loop.
Return j = 2: the last index of the left range.
Partition complete. The left range [7, 3, 2] is still unsorted.
